title: What Jewellery to Wear with an Anarkali: A Guide by Neckline
excerpt: How to pair earrings, necklaces and bangles with an Anarkali suit, matched to the neckline, the embroidery and the occasion, so the look feels balanced.
body:
The right jewellery for an Anarkali depends mostly on the neckline. A high or heavily embroidered neckline calls for statement earrings and no necklace, while a deep round or V neck leaves room for a choker or layered piece. Get that one choice right and the rest of the look falls into place.

## The golden rule: one hero piece

An Anarkali is already a dramatic outfit. The flare, the dupatta and the embroidery all ask for attention. So choose one hero, either the earrings or the necklace, and keep everything else quieter.

If your Anarkali has gota or zari work around the neckline, that work is already acting as a necklace. Let your earrings be the star. If the neckline is plain, a necklace can carry the look and your earrings can be small studs or drops.

## Pairing by neckline

| Neckline | Earrings | Necklace | Bangles |
|---|---|---|---|
| High or band collar | Long chandbalis or shoulder-duster jhumkas | Skip it | A few slim bangles |
| Round neck, embroidered | Medium jhumkas or chandbalis | Skip it or a very fine chain | One statement kada |
| Round neck, plain | Small drops or studs | Choker or short layered necklace | Stacked thin bangles |
| Deep V or sweetheart | Small to medium drops | Long necklace or V-shaped pendant set | Light stack |
| Boat neck | Statement earrings | Skip it | Kada or cuff |
| Square neck | Medium jhumkas | Short square or collar necklace | Thin bangles |

Use this as a starting point, not a rulebook. A tall woman with a long neck can carry long earrings and a choker together; on a petite frame the same pairing can feel crowded.

## Metal and stone by colour

**Gold and antique gold** suit warm, rich colours such as royal blue, maroon, mustard and bottle green. They also suit any outfit with gold gota. The [Royal Blue Georgette Anarkali Suit Set](/products/royal-blue-georgette-anarkali-suit-gota-handwork-dupatta/) with gold jhumkas is a classic festive pairing.

**Pearls and kundan** soften pastels. Lavender, mint, sage and powder pink look fresh and modern with pearl drops or a kundan choker. The [Lavender Taffeta Silk Gota Work Anarkali Suit Set](/products/lavender-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-organza-dupatta/) is a good example: pearls keep it graceful, while heavy gold could overpower the colour.

**Silver and oxidised silver** work with ivory, black, indigo and cotton prints. They give a more relaxed, earthy look, lovely for a daytime mehendi or a casual festive lunch.

**Polki and emeralds** sit beautifully against green and ivory. Try them with a sage or mint Anarkali for a wedding.

## Matching jewellery to the occasion

**Daytime functions and pooja:** keep it light. Small jhumkas, a few bangles and maybe a maang tikka if you love one. Heavy sets in daylight can look like too much.

**Evening parties and Diwali:** this is when chandbalis, kundan and polki shine. Evening light picks up stones and gold beautifully.

**Weddings and receptions:** you can wear a full set, but still follow the one-hero rule. If you choose a heavy necklace, keep the earrings smaller. For more ideas, browse our [wedding guest outfits](/indian-wedding-guest-outfits/).

## Bangles, rings and the finishing touches

Bangles add sound and movement, which suits the swing of an Anarkali. With full sleeves, choose one kada or a thin stack worn over the cuff. With three-quarter sleeves, you have space for a fuller stack on one or both wrists.

A single cocktail ring on the hand without bangles balances the look. A maang tikka is a lovely extra for weddings, especially if your hair is in a centre parting and your earrings are not too long.

Do not forget the dupatta. If it is heavy, like the sequin organza piece with the [Sage Green Taffeta Silk Gota Work Anarkali Suit Set](/products/sage-green-taffeta-silk-gota-work-anarkali-suit-set-with-sequin-organza-dupatta/), keep the necklace minimal so the two do not compete across your shoulders.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Wearing a heavy necklace and long statement earrings together with an embroidered neckline.
- Mixing gold and silver tones in one look without a clear reason.
- Choosing jewellery that catches on organza or net dupattas. Smooth backs and closed settings are safer.
- Forgetting comfort. Very heavy earrings can be painful after a few hours of dancing, so test them at home first.

## Frequently asked questions

**Should I wear a necklace with an Anarkali?**
Only if the neckline is plain or deep. If the neckline has embroidery or gota work, skip the necklace and wear statement earrings instead.

**What earrings suit an Anarkali best?**
Jhumkas and chandbalis are the most popular because their round, traditional shapes echo the flare of the outfit.

**Can I wear pearls with a dark Anarkali?**
Yes. Pearls look elegant with navy, black and bottle green, especially in an evening setting.

**What jewellery suits a pastel Anarkali?**
Pearls, kundan and light polki work best. They keep the soft colour in focus.
